title: kate-ui: give a carriage return no width
summary: visual_row_count gives a carriage return a width of 0. A tab still uses the tab width. The test goes in the existing layout tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: fn visual_row_count(line: &str, columns: u32, tab_width: u8) -> u32

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: layout.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Keep visual_row_count pub(crate). Change only the loop body. Use one if else if. Do not nest an if inside an if. if scalar == '\t' { width = width.saturating_add(step - (width % step)); } else if scalar != '\r' { width = width.saturating_add(1); }. A carriage return adds nothing. Do not touch notice_from, visible_line_range, or span_line_window. The existing tests visual_row_count_splits_a_long_line and a_tab_uses_the_tab_width stay green. The test a_carriage_return_has_no_width calls visual_row_count of ab, a carriage return, cd with columns 4 and tab width 4 and gets 1. abcd with columns 4 and tab width 4 stays 1. One tab with columns 4 and tab width 4 stays 1. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: layout::tests::a_carriage_return_has_no_width
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. ab, a carriage return, cd at 4 columns has 2 rows. After the change it has 1 row. abcd stays 1 row. One tab at width 4 stays 1 row.
